# BrightSword Copilot Instructions

## Repository overview

.NET 10 monorepo producing 5 NuGet packages that ship together at a **unified suite version** (currently 2.0.0):

| Package | Purpose |
|---------|---------|
| `BrightSword.SwissKnife` | Utility classes and extension methods (monads, reflection, collections, strings) |
| `BrightSword.Crucible` | Unit testing utilities for MSTest (`ExpectException<T>`) |
| `BrightSword.Feber` | Automated delegate generation via LINQ Expression trees |
| `BrightSword.Squid` | Runtime type emission via System.Reflection.Emit |
| `BrightSword.Packages` | Metapackage bundling all four libraries above |

Test projects: `BrightSword.SwissKnife.Tests`, `BrightSword.Feber.Tests`, `BrightSword.Squid.Tests` (xUnit).
Sample app: `BrightSword.Feber.SamplesApp`.

## Build commands

The canonical build entrypoint is `Build.proj`. Always use it instead of `dotnet build` on individual projects.

```bash
# Full CI-equivalent (clean, restore, build, test, pack)
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:CI /p:Configuration=Release /v:minimal

# Build and test only (faster iteration)
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:"Restore;BuildPackages;BuildTests;Test" /p:Configuration=Release

# Run a single test project
dotnet test BrightSword.SwissKnife.Tests/BrightSword.SwissKnife.Tests.csproj -c Release

# Run a single test by name
dotnet test BrightSword.Feber.Tests/BrightSword.Feber.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "Print_WritesToConsole"

# Pack all packages
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:Pack /p:Configuration=Release

# Pack a single project
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:PackSingle /p:Configuration=Release;Package=BrightSword.SwissKnife
```

> **PowerShell note**: Quote multi-target `/t:"Restore;BuildPackages"` — semicolons are interpreted by the shell otherwise.

## Versioning

All 5 packages share a **single `VersionPrefix`** in the root `version.props`. There are no per-project version files.

```bash
# Bump patch (2.0.0 → 2.0.1) — applies to all packages
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:IncrementVersion /p:Level=Patch

# Bump and git-commit locally
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:IncrementVersion /p:Level=Patch /p:Commit=true
```

The `IncrementVersion` target calls `scripts/increment-version.ps1` (not inline PowerShell — inline MSBuild `Exec` has severe quoting issues on .NET Core).

A `-preview` version suffix is appended automatically unless `GITHUB_REF_TYPE=tag`.

## Key files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Build.proj` | Centralized MSBuild targets (Restore, Build, Test, Pack, CI, IncrementVersion) |
| `version.props` | Single suite `VersionPrefix` + per-package `PackageId`/metadata |
| `versioning.targets` | `IncrementVersion` MSBuild target |
| `Directory.Build.props` | Shared build config: net10.0, nullable, SourceLink, packaging defaults |
| `package-dependencies.json` | Dependency graph manifest (generated by `scripts/generate-package-dependencies.ps1`) |
| `scripts/generate-docs.ps1` | Jekyll docs site generator (produces `artifacts/docs` with front matter) |
| `scripts/increment-version.ps1` | PowerShell script that edits `version.props` XML |

## CI/CD workflows

| Workflow | Trigger | Purpose |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `ci.yml` | Push to main/develop/feature/fix/release, PRs to main | Calls `build-and-test.yml` reusable workflow |
| `build-and-test.yml` | Called by `ci.yml` | Restore → Build → Test → Generate docs |
| `pr-validation.yml` | PRs to main | Lightweight PR validation |
| `publish-packages.yml` | Tag push `v*` or manual dispatch | Packs and publishes all 5 packages to NuGet |
| `gh-pages.yml` | Push to main | Generates Jekyll docs, deploys to gh-pages branch |
| `pack.yml` | Reusable | Pack individual projects |

**Release process**: Push a `v*` tag (e.g. `v2.0.1`) → `publish-packages.yml` publishes all 5 packages. All packages always publish together.

## Documentation

- GitHub Pages: https://johnazariah.github.io/brightsword/ (Jekyll with `just-the-docs` theme)
- `scripts/generate-docs.ps1` produces a Jekyll site in `artifacts/docs` with `_config.yml` and front matter on all markdown files
- Per-project docs live in `<Project>/docs/` folders and are copied into the Jekyll site
- Top-level `docs/` contains architecture, build, CI/CD, versioning, and contributing guides

```bash
# Generate docs locally
dotnet msbuild Build.proj /t:"Restore;BuildPackages" /p:Configuration=Release
pwsh ./scripts/generate-docs.ps1
# Verify: artifacts/docs/index.md and artifacts/docs/_config.yml should exist
```

## Testing conventions

- **508 tests** across 3 test projects, >85% line and branch coverage
- Test framework: xUnit with `[Fact]` and `[Theory]`
- Test naming: `MethodName_Scenario_ExpectedBehavior` (underscores accepted, CA1707 suppressed in test projects)
- `InternalsVisibleTo` is used to test internal APIs
- **Thread safety**: Any test that redirects `Console.Out` via `Console.SetOut()` **must** lock `Console.Out` or use `[Collection]` to prevent parallel xUnit runners from interfering. `Console.SetOut` is not thread-safe — parallel tests can restore the original `TextWriter` mid-operation, causing partial output capture.

## Known gotchas (learned from production issues)

### GitHub Actions

1. **jq in bash**: Always quote the full jq filter — `jq -r '.permission // empty'` not `jq -r .permission // empty`. Bash interprets `//` as path separators.

2. **peaceiris/actions-gh-pages + Jekyll**: Must set `enable_jekyll: true` to prevent `.nojekyll` from being created. Without this, GitHub Pages won't process markdown files (only serves pre-built HTML). Also use `force_orphan: true` when publishing to an orphan gh-pages branch.

3. **persist-credentials on checkout**: Do NOT use `persist-credentials: false` if the workflow needs to push (e.g. to gh-pages). The GITHUB_TOKEN needs the persisted credentials to authenticate git operations.

### NuGet packaging

4. **Duplicate README.md**: When `PackageReadmeFile=README.md` is set in `Directory.Build.props` AND a `docs/README.md` is included with `Pack="true" PackagePath=""`, both get packed to the package root causing a NuGet 400 "duplicated files" error. Fix: condition the docs inclusion on `!Exists('README.md')` (already applied in `Directory.Build.props` line 57).

5. **Metapackage warnings**: `BrightSword.Packages` uses `IncludeBuildOutput=false` which triggers expected NU5128 warning (no lib assemblies) and snupkg push fails with "no symbol files". Both are harmless for metapackages.

### MSBuild

6. **Inline PowerShell in MSBuild Exec**: Never use inline PowerShell with nested quotes in MSBuild `<Exec>` tasks — it causes severe quoting issues that silently corrupt output files. Always use a separate `.ps1` file called via `pwsh -File script.ps1`.

## Architecture

```
BrightSword.Packages (metapackage)
├── BrightSword.SwissKnife    (no internal dependencies)
├── BrightSword.Crucible      (no internal dependencies)
├── BrightSword.Feber          → depends on SwissKnife
└── BrightSword.Squid          → depends on SwissKnife
```

- **SwissKnife**: Foundation layer — monadic extensions (`Maybe`, `When`, `MakeSafe`), collection helpers, string tokenization, reflection utilities, sequential GUID, command-line framework
- **Crucible**: Test helpers — `ExpectException<T>` for MSTest exception assertions
- **Feber**: Expression tree code generation — builds compiled delegates for property copying, comparison, serialization, pretty-printing. First call reflects + JIT compiles; subsequent calls use cached delegate (<0.001ms)
- **Squid**: IL emit code generation — `Dynamic<T>.NewInstance()` creates concrete DTO types from interfaces at runtime using `System.Reflection.Emit`
